title: Grouped Data v1

findings.finding: Practice requires a frequency polygon before its construction has been introduced.
findings.breakdown: The histogram example does not identify which points a polygon joins. Students could plausibly join bar corners instead of bar-top centres.
findings.checked: The complete teaching through p8 demonstrates histograms and class centres, but no frequency polygon. Practice solution figures do not supply preceding instruction.
findings.assumptions: Coordinate plotting is prior knowledge; the frequency-polygon convention requires introduction. Calculator use is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Overlay a frequency polygon on p8-example-graph-response. State: 'Plot each class centre against its frequency and join consecutive points with straight lines. Finish at frequency 0, one class width before the first centre and one class width after the last centre.' Show (−3,0), (2,3), (7,7), (12,15), (17,19), (22,6), (27,0).

findings.doneWhen: A demonstrated polygon identifies its centre-based points and endpoints before p9-q1.

findings.finding: Cumulative frequencies and ogive construction are first required without instruction; later construction tasks depend on the same missing method.
findings.breakdown: Students must calculate running totals and place ogive points at upper class edges rather than class centres. The later median teaching explains reading a supplied ogive, not constructing one.
findings.checked: No supplied teaching introduces running totals or cumulative graph construction. p10-q2 requests these constructions but contains no instructional hint. p12 models median reading only. One introduction before p10-q2 addresses the shared cause.
findings.assumptions: Addition and coordinate plotting are prior knowledge. Cumulative graph construction is new within the supplied complete teaching.

repair.proposal: Before p10-q2-a, demonstrate classes 0–4, 5–9, 10–14 with frequencies 2, 3, 1. State: 'Cumulative frequency is the running total: 2, 2+3=5, 5+1=6. Draw cumulative histogram bars with heights 2, 5, 6. For an ogive, start at frequency 0 on the left edge of the first bar, then join the upper-right corners with straight lines.' Label the class edges and show (−0.5,0), (4.5,2), (9.5,5), (14.5,6).

findings.doneWhen: Before p10-q2, students see running totals, class-edge placement and the ogive construction demonstrated together; later tasks can refer back to this example.

findings.finding: Graphical IQR is assigned without connecting the quartiles to cumulative-frequency heights.
findings.breakdown: The median example demonstrates the 50% position only. Students receive no explicit connection from the lower and upper quartiles to N/4 and 3N/4 on the cumulative-frequency axis before being asked to read and subtract their score values.
findings.checked: Checked all preceding teaching and practice. p12-teaching and p12-example-demonstration establish median reading, but no preceding prompt models or cues either graphical quartile position. Prior knowledge of quartiles and IQR does not itself establish their use on the newly introduced cumulative graph.
findings.assumptions: Quartiles and IQR are prior knowledge from the separately taught Quartiles and Box Plots content. The missing component is applying them to cumulative-frequency graphs. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Before p18-q11, add: 'For an ogive with total frequency N, locate Q1 at cumulative frequency N/4 and Q3 at cumulative frequency 3N/4. Read their score values using horizontal then vertical guides, as for the median. Estimate IQR = Q3 − Q1.'

findings.doneWhen: Students receive the cumulative-frequency positions and reading route for both quartiles before independently estimating graphical IQR.

findings.finding: Follow the zero-frequency class with a numerical extension showing how additional observations affect running totals.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up exposes why every subsequent cumulative total includes observations added to an earlier class.
findings.checked: Adding three observations to 30–39 changes 4,7,9,9,10,12,17 to 4,7,9,12,13,15,20. It uses the cumulative-frequency method required in this topic.
findings.assumptions: Use after the cumulative-frequency introduction proposed in the merged construction finding.

repair.proposal: After p10-q2-b add optional parts: 'c. Three additional observations lie in the 30–39 class. Write the new cumulative frequencies.' Answer: 4, 7, 9, 12, 13, 15, 20. 'd. Which cumulative frequencies increased by 3? Explain why.' Answer: Those for 30–39, 40–49, 50–59 and 60–69, because each running total includes the three additional observations.

findings.doneWhen: The optional follow-up uses the existing table and separates its two questions into parts.

findings.finding: Extend the height question to connect a common increase in representative values with the increase in estimated mean.
findings.breakdown: Shifting every class by the same amount preserves frequencies and increases the estimated mean by that amount.
findings.checked: The original weighted total is 17490 for 100 students. Adding 2 cm to each centre adds 200 to the weighted total, giving 17690/100 = 176.9 cm.
findings.assumptions: The shifted classes retain the same students and frequencies, as the proposed prompt specifies.

repair.proposal: After p14-q3-b add optional parts: 'c. One year later, every student is exactly 2 cm taller. Use the same groups shifted up by 2 cm. What is the new estimated mean height?' Answer: 176.9 cm. 'd. How much has the estimated mean increased?' Answer: 2 cm.

findings.doneWhen: The numerical follow-up explicitly shifts the groups and retains their frequencies.

findings.finding: Question 11 moves from constructing and reading grouped tables directly to reconstructing class frequencies from mixed cumulative statements.
findings.breakdown: Students must distinguish nested counts, subtract them to recover an interval frequency, and subtract two disjoint tails from the total. Earlier questions practise adding existing classes, but none separately rehearses these reconstruction decisions before they are combined.
findings.checked: Checked all teaching and the preceding practice, including p4-q2-c, p5-q5-b, p6-q8 and p7-q10. These establish totals and combined frequencies, but provide neither reconstruction bridge. Although Question 11 closes the exercise, the preceding questions do not build towards its combined demands.
findings.assumptions: Ordinary subtraction and totals are established. Calculator availability does not affect the reasoning demand.

repair.proposal: Immediately before Question 11, insert: (a) 'Of 50 people, 12 received 10 or fewer emails and 31 received 20 or fewer emails. How many received more than 10 but no more than 20 emails?' Answer: 19. (b) 'Of 50 people, 12 received 10 or fewer emails and 9 received more than 20 emails. How many received more than 10 but no more than 20 emails?' Answer: 29.

findings.doneWhen: Students separately practise subtracting nested counts and subtracting two disjoint tails before combining those decisions in Question 11.

findings.finding: The first histogram practice requires frequency polygons, but preceding teaching models only a histogram.
findings.breakdown: Students have no model for locating polygon points at class centres, joining them, retaining a zero-frequency class, or choosing the closing points.
findings.checked: The complete teaching contains no frequency-polygon construction. p8-information-block and p8-example-root explain class centres and histogram construction only. The completed practice graphs are answer-only and cannot supply preceding instruction.
findings.assumptions: General graph construction is prior knowledge; grouped frequency-polygon construction is not established by the supplied teaching. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Extend p8-example-root by plotting (2,3), (7,7), (12,15), (17,19) and (22,6) on its histogram and joining consecutive points. Close the polygon at (-3,0) and (27,0), the centres of the adjacent outside classes. State that a zero-frequency class must still have a point at its centre with height zero.

findings.doneWhen: Before p9-q1-a, teaching shows how to choose the polygon points and closing points, including the treatment of a zero-frequency class.

findings.finding: Cumulative-frequency construction and its reversal are required without teaching the relationship between ordinary frequencies, cumulative totals and ogive points.
findings.breakdown: Students first need running totals and upper-boundary plotting in p10-q2. Later questions reuse that construction, and p23-q20-b requires reversing cumulative totals to recover class frequencies. The median teaching explains how to read a supplied ogive, rather than how to construct or reverse it.
findings.checked: Checked the complete teaching and intervening practice. p7-q11 requests reconstruction but supplies no instructional method. p8 models an ordinary histogram; p10 independently assigns cumulative construction. p12 models median reading only. Neither the earlier assignments nor their answer-only solutions supply the missing teaching.
findings.assumptions: Ordinary grouped histograms, addition and subtraction are established. Cumulative-frequency construction is a new variant here. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Before p10-q2, reuse the p8 table. Model cumulative totals 3, 10, 25, 44, 50, explaining that each counts all observations through the current class. Draw cumulative bars with those heights and an ogive through (-0.5,0), (4.5,3), (9.5,10), (14.5,25), (19.5,44), (24.5,50). Explain that the points use upper class boundaries, rather than class centres, and that a zero-frequency class leaves the total unchanged. Add the reverse calculation: 'The frequency of 10–14 is 25−10=15: subtract the preceding cumulative total.'

findings.doneWhen: Before the first independent cumulative construction, students see running totals, cumulative bars, upper-boundary ogive points and recovery of an ordinary frequency by subtraction.

findings.finding: The topic explicitly builds on calculating a mean from an ungrouped frequency table, but does not rehearse that prior method.
findings.breakdown: The grouped-mean example requires weighting values by their frequencies and dividing by total frequency. Students who instead average the row values or divide by the number of classes have no opening review to expose that misunderstanding before class centres are introduced.
findings.checked: p11-mean-definition explicitly identifies the ungrouped frequency-table calculation as prior knowledge. Earlier teaching and the immediately preceding histogram exercise do not rehearse it. p8-review-block covers midpoints only. The grouped-mean definition supplies the new procedure but does not provide retrieval practice of the prior frequency-table method.
findings.assumptions: Ungrouped frequency-table means are prior knowledge, consistent with the stated course library. A calculator is assumed; numerical evaluation is not the missing review piece.

repair.proposal: Before p11-mean-definition, add three short review items: (a) 'Scores 2, 5, 8 have frequencies 3, 2, 1. How many scores are there?' Answer: 6. (b) 'For that table, find the total of all scores.' Answer: 24. (c) 'Scores 1, 4, 7 have frequencies 2, 1, 3. Find the mean.' Answer: 4.5. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The opening review rehearses weighting values and dividing by total frequency before applying that structure to class centres.

protectedGroups.observation: Representing the same observations in two ways makes the loss of individual-value frequencies directly visible.
protectedGroups.varies: Whether values are listed separately or combined into classes.
protectedGroups.invariant: The raw handspan data and total number of observations.

protectedGroups.observation: Students must distinguish which endpoint is included rather than associate inequality classes with one fixed endpoint convention.
protectedGroups.varies: The included endpoint, numerical bounds and variable.
protectedGroups.invariant: A bounded interval with one included endpoint, matched to a verbal description.

protectedGroups.observation: The supplied class-centre scaffold is removed while the same histogram-and-polygon task is retained.
protectedGroups.varies: Class centres change from supplied to student-calculated; the second dataset also includes an empty class.
protectedGroups.invariant: Five equal-width classes represented by a histogram and frequency polygon.

protectedGroups.observation: Doubling all frequencies preserves the estimated mean; doubling class values doubles it.
protectedGroups.varies: First the frequency multiplier, then the class-value multiplier.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing the frequency at a class centre equal to the estimated mean leaves that mean unchanged.
protectedGroups.varies: Only the frequency of the class centred at 50.

protectedGroups.observation: Increasing every class value by one increases the estimated mean by one.
protectedGroups.varies: Every class endpoint increases by one.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing grouping can preserve or change the mean estimate.
protectedGroups.varies: The subdivision or merging of the upper classes.
protectedGroups.invariant: Total frequency and the lower occupied classes.

notReliablyReviewed.reason: Page 24 is not among the attached images. Its diagram specification supports identifying the intended methods, but the actual graph could not be inspected.

importReview: Lean content review table: 47 of 47 blocks passed.

sequences.title: Mean and median from grouped data

dropped.reason: The final question is a supported closing challenge rather than a substantial unsupported transition. Earlier questions combine class frequencies into lower and upper totals; q11 reverses that relationship using ordinary subtraction. Its counts and total explicitly supply all required information. A new named cumulative-frequency construction is not needed.

candidates.finding: The statements “30 people said they received 10 or fewer emails” and “45 people received 20 or fewer emails” introduce recovery of class frequencies from cumulative counts without teaching that method.

dropped.reason: Earlier practice p7-q11 already rehearses recovering disjoint class frequencies by subtracting overlapping totals. p10-q2 subsequently connects ordinary frequencies with cumulative totals. Recovering frequencies from cumulative bar heights combines those preceding demands; it does not establish a new unsupported method.

candidates.finding: 'By completing the table, calculate the mean house price' requires ordinary frequencies to be recovered from cumulative bar heights, a reversal not previously taught.
